fieldMarks: Long, pointed ear tufts (tassels) on the ears.
The Kaibab squirrel (S. a. kaibabensis) is one of nine subspecies and was formerly treated as a separate species.
behavior: Feeds on ponderosa pine seeds (preferred), inner bark of young twigs, buds and fungi; in winter clips roughly 45 twigs a day, leaving clipped twigs under pines.
Builds nests of pine twigs high in the crown (about 16–90 ft up), usually on the south side of the tree.
Summer home ranges average about 18 acres; winter ranges are smaller.
habitat: Nearly confined to cool, dry ponderosa pine forest, typically between 5,500 and 8,500 ft elevation; optimum habitat is all-aged ponderosa pine stands.
range: Colorado Plateau and southern Rocky Mountains of Colorado, Utah, Arizona and New Mexico, south into Mexico's Sierra Madre Occidental; not in Canada. Transplanted populations are established in Arizona's Graham and Santa Catalina mountains.
